Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. A swarm of bees clustered tight and still on the wet grass at the top of a low rise, at the edge of a flooded water meadow on the floor of a broad river valley, at first light on a cold morning in early spring, before the sun is up, seen from low in the grass a few paces off. A swarm of bees, wasps and the small pollinating things. No single shape, no face, no chief insect. All of it together fills a doorway: a swarm that could not be walked through without it parting. A single part, a fifth of it, fills a hat. It may be divided into as many as five such parts. Spread loose across a field it can look like a thin haze. Drawn tight it is about the size of a barrel a person could carry. Mostly it is nothing a passer-by would notice: bees working a field in an order that looks like a plan. If someone stands still, the swarm gathers around them and waits. It does not attack and does not speak. Up close, when it is spoken to, all the bees turn the same way, like a crowd leaning toward a sound. It carries nothing but what bees carry: pollen, nectar, wax scraps. In the player's words: "Mortals will meet me as weather in the flowers, not as a face." "It is polite in the way weather is polite." Seen from behind or in deep shadow, the head turned away or lost in darkness, no face visible. It is insects and nothing else: it has no head, no body and no figure, and it forms none. Here, in the cold, it is drawn tight, a close-packed cluster about the size of a barrel, with no insect in the air. The light is the grey of first light, cold and low, and the one strong light in the picture is a blue light low in the sky to the left of center, steady and larger than the moon, standing a little above the skyline, bright enough to throw a faint blue shadow from the cluster across the wet grass and to lie as a cool gleam on the floodwater. Near the viewer: wet grass, standing floodwater, and a hedge laid by hand some years ago, with hazel catkins and the first blackthorn blossom just breaking. In the middle distance: more water meadow, flooded in places, hedged fields and bare, pruned orchards on the lower slopes, old woods in the side valleys with snow still lying in their shade. Far off, on the skyline, a long edge of high brown heather upland, and one thin thread of woodsmoke rising a few miles away with nothing to be seen of the place it rises from. No people, no animals, no buildings, no road or track. The small cluster on the rise beneath the wide valley and the blue light gives the scale.
